releases.body: 3.2.0 — The Claude Code plugin now bundles the MCP server: claude plugin install tincan@tincan starts Tin Can through npx, pinned to this release, with no global install. Its tools appear as mcp__plugin_tincan_tincan__*; tincan mcp install remains the route to the short mcp__tincan__* names. Use one or the other, not both. The plugin needs Node and npm on PATH. Every tool now carries a standard MCP title and annotations (read-only, idempotent, local-only), and integer parameters are advertised as integers. No address format or tool interface change.

3.1.0 — Add opt-in strict pull inboxes with operator grants, quarantine and release controls, identity-bound retrieval, durable retries, and body-free auditing. Preserve native delivery for receivers without strict mode. Restart existing Tin Can connections after upgrading.

3.0.0 — Bind Codex sender identity to MCP request metadata. Refuse ambiguous senders and keep unknown project directories unknown. Canonical replies now match runtime, full durable ID and machine independently of the display name. Address syntax is unchanged; consumers implementing resolution must adopt the updated contract fixture. Existing servers must restart to load this fix. Adds concurrent-request and stdio regression coverage.

2.6.1 — Mail routing is now configured rather than built in: $TINCAN_HOME/mail-routing.json names the recipient file, the inbox command, the command's own sender name and any prefixes to deliver directly; with no recipient file nothing is routed. The method reported for a filed message is now `mailbox`. Adds scripts/check-public.sh and a pre-push hook (git config core.hooksPath .githooks) that blocks pushing home paths, email addresses, credentials or terms from a local list. Docs and test fixtures use generic names. No address format change.

2.6.0 — Mail routing: direct messages to one designated session can be filed with an inbox command instead of being delivered into it. Superseded by 2.6.1, which takes the recipient and the inbox command from configuration ($TINCAN_HOME/mail-routing.json) and reports the method as `mailbox`; upgrade to 2.6.1. See docs/mail-routing.md. No address format change.

issues.title: Short names as addresses: the prefix trap is the single-machine version, and cross-machine delivery widens it to every crossing
Refuse a bare name that is also the stem of a longer live name, rather than resolving it (address-format change, major)
Document canonical_id as the address form that cannot misroute, and record the prefix trap as a known limitation
Note for @berkay-byte: PR "test: keep CLI help flags in parity" was lost in the 2.0.0 republish
`peers` serves a dead record for a live session, while the live one is not served — and the envelope disagrees with it
